peerMapping.justification: This is a long BE versus short peer basket construction with a separate SP500 market hedge. The basket favors business models tied to firm onsite power, grid scarcity, and AI data-center load growth rather than the memory and semiconductor manufacturing names that dominate the universe. Weights sum to exactly 1 and are highest for TSLA and NBIS because their economics are closest to power-constrained infrastructure; NVDA is meaningful but less direct; GOOGL and MSFT are demand-side references only. All peer weights respect displayed 24-hour perp liquidity in USD millions: each chosen peer is above BE's 0.582 USD millions, and lower-comparability or more diversified names receive smaller weights.

peers.name: Tesla
peers.reason: TSLA is the closest economic adjacency because it contains energy storage and clean-energy hardware alongside vehicles, and it also has the strongest displayed 24-hour perp liquidity among the chosen peers at 4.551 USD millions, so it receives the largest peer weight.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: NVDA is included as a high-liquidity proxy for the AI data-center demand cycle that drives interest in Bloom Energy's onsite power systems; its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 3.384 USD millions, supporting the second-largest weight.

peers.name: Nebius Group
peers.reason: AI cloud and data-center capacity make power procurement and energization timing central to the equity story, similar to BE's onsite power pitch for data centers; displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 2.35 USD millions.

peers.name: Alphabet
peers.reason: GOOGL represents the hyperscale data-center customer side of the same power-demand theme, but it is a more diversified advertising and software business, and its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 2.262 USD millions; therefore it receives the smallest weight.

peers.name: Microsoft
peers.reason: Microsoft is another hyperscaler whose data-center expansion drives demand for reliable onsite power, an indirect but real economic linkage to Bloom Energy. Displayed 24-hour perp liquidity of 1.386 USD millions is adequate for a moderate weight.

primary_index_hedge.name: S&P 500
primary_index_hedge.reason: SP500 is the broad US equity beta hedge and has the deepest displayed 24-hour perp liquidity among the eligible equity_index and equity_etf rows at 30.814 USD millions, large relative to BE at 0.582 USD millions; the broader index also avoids over-hedging the specific AI and memory factor already represented in the peer basket.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted and remaining weights renormalized once at least three peers exist; basket rebased to the target spot level at the first overlapping date

liveSplice.method: current TradeXYZ perp mid divided by each peer's latest USD cash close; available Kimi weights renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot close

earningsOptions.source: consolidated listed-options chain, verified earnings calendars, and split-adjusted price history

liquidityFilter.sides: OTM puts below spot and OTM calls above spot

model.name: liquid vertical-spread risk-neutral CDF
model.description: Liquid vertical spreads are used when the chain supplies at least four valid probability points; otherwise the nearest liquid ATM straddle supplies the expiration distribution. Earnings-date log distances are time-scaled from the first post-event expiration.
model.measure: risk-neutral, not a historical or physical forecast

historicalAnalysis.eventSource: SEC earnings release history with verified calendar fallback
historicalAnalysis.method: Each current two-leg structure is translated into percentage-of-spot strikes and debit. Those same normalized strikes and today's debit percentage are replayed across prior earnings using the same calendar-day entry lead and post-event exit horizon. A profitable event requires expiration payoff greater than the original debit.
historicalAnalysis.limitation: Stock-path proxy using today's premium; historical option quotes, bid-ask execution, volatility repricing, early exercise, dividends, and transaction costs are not reconstructed.
